newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures mixed in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures mixed in nervous trade.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mixed in nervous trade after another mighty dollar move overnight.
September marks and Swiss francs fell to new contract lows overnight of $0.5303 and $0.6529, respectively, before drifting up from those levels in early pit trade.
September marks, yen and Swiss turned higher in early trade, bouncing from the overnight losses.

"Volatility kind of shot up overnight, so it's a little bit nervous right now," an IMM currency futures trader said. "We're either going to start retracing or we're going to hit some new highs in the dollar."

The dollar hit a new 94-month high of 1.8913 marks before a morning spate of profit taking set in, traders said. Dollar/yen remained solidly above 119.00, a level now seen as support, with upside targets of 121.00 and 122.00 yen, they added.
Several traders gave little credence to the currency bounce early Wednesday, saying bearish currency sentiment persists.
"They have a lot of recovering to do" to change the currency trend, the currency trader said. "This is a little bit of an intraday play," he added.

Overnight mark weakness was tied to a July German unemployment report that showed a mildly weaker labor market than expected and to comments overnight that Bonn sees no reason to change its foreign exchange stance.
Dollar bulls were also encouraged by signs the Bundesbank cannot raise its securities repurchase rate enough to defend the mark in the current German economic climate.

September sterling was sharply lower, though off its lows, after falling through $1.59 support overnight. Traders cited technicals and fears the Bank of England will not raise interest rates Thursday.
Still, some analysts expect a 25-basis-point BOE rate hike Thursday.
September yen was slightly higher in pit session trade, also after losses overnight.

Traders noted passing attention to comments overnight from U.S. presidential advisor Fred Bergsten, who said the dollar was overvalued at its present level, particularly versus the yen and European currencies.

At 0910 CDT/1410 GMT, Sept yen was up $0.000014 at $0.008444, marks rose $0.0001 to $0.5337, Swiss francs rose $0.0009 to $0.6561, sterling was down $0.0240 to $1.5968, Canadian dollars were off $0.0015 to $0.7246, Australian dollars were $0.0047 lower to $0.7355, and Mexican pesos climbed $0.000300 to $0.126550.
